chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Baseer said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about their office-bearers (or: their actions/positions), so he (peace be upon him) said to me: O Abu Muhammad! No, and not (even) for a mark of a pen. Indeed, one of you would not attain anything from their world except that they would take from his religion an equivalent amount, or he said: Until he loses from his religion an equivalent amount.

key_terms.مَدَّةَ قَلَمٍ: A mark of a pen (a very small amount)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of serving in the Umayyad government according to Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of 'dunya for din' (worldly gain for religious loss), warning that accepting official positions under Umayyad rulers entails a spiritual transaction where worldly benefits are offset by a corresponding loss in religious integrity. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of political legitimacy, where serving the unjust ruler compromises one's religious standing, a theme deeply connected to the Quranic warning against taking disbelievers as allies over believers.
